correctness.rationale: Sine eigenvectors with arm coefficients summing to zero give k independent (m-1)-dimensional kernel subspaces. For ell>=2k-1, positivity of elementary symmetric sums and tree-walk parity makes every required off-diagonal polynomial entry nonzero; for (k,ell)=(3,4),(4,5),(4,6), direct exact expansions and degree-sum walks do the same. At larger distance polynomial entries vanish. Thus the constructed symmetric exact-support matrix proves M>=k(m-1); the explicit source forcing sequence gives Z<=k(m-1) and standard M<=Z closes equality. The 108 small spectral/witness cases and 91,793 exhaustive smaller seed tests are nonproof checks; no extrapolation is used.

value.rationale: The original 2026 source formulates the sharp spider bound as an open all-parameter conjecture after proving only an upper bound. This proof gives all cube and fourth-power instances for every number of arms and permissible length, plus all higher powers in an unbounded long-arm parameter region, as well as exact real symmetric maximum nullity/minimum rank via a constructive spectral matrix.
